purpose: P0 consistency fixture for the dsh-native Zig harness: drive initialize/newSession/prompt(plain), replay one model call, compare the normalized v4 session log.

v3Session.note: Committed, already-tokenized v3 projection. It is a scripted fake-ACP log, not a real dsh turn: 6 lines, stops at assistant/attempt, has no user/message, inbox splice, request/context, step/end or turn/end.

v3Behavior.note: Raw scripted parent log (seq/time present, SYS PROMPT, tool schema t1). The committed session.v3.jsonl is its normalized projection.

v4GroundTruth.note: Real, normalized v4 plain-text turn. Used for v4 envelope, event order and field shapes. Its provider is deepseek-official and it includes SDK-only plugins (runtime context, title, delivery, feedback); those are excluded below.

scenarioConfig.note: plain-turn scenario: hasModelTurn, recorded, headerClass main, DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=never, workspace seeded with seed.txt.

v3ToV4Differences.change: Session header version 3 -> 4; same required/optional field set.
Committed fixtures omit the physical seq/time envelope; createdAt and stream clocks are zeroed before comparison.
system/message source {kind:plugin, plugin:@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt} becomes {kind:system-prompt}; v4 rejects kind:plugin.

The scripted v3 assistant/attempt becomes a successful v4 assistant/message with message content, source, id and surfaceOp append. assistant/attempt remains a v4 event, but only for attempts that commit no surface message.

The completed assistant/message stream gains a terminal raw finish chunk after the packed text-chunks row. The v3 attempt stream has only text-chunks; the real v4 assistant/message records the finish chunk, and llm-replay refuses a recorded call without a finish chunk.
Real v4 sessions start with permission/preset, sandbox/mode and approval/policy before the first turn. These are runtime plugin events, not format-migration events; the v3 scripted log omits them.
The prompt is inserted into next-turn before turn/start and removed after turn/start. The v3 scripted log has neither event.
The claimed prompt is appended as a user/message on the surface before request/header. The v3 scripted log omits it.
A real v4 first request also appends request/context with the resolved route metadata after request/header. The v3 scripted log omits it.
The completed turn closes with step/end and turn/end reason completed after assistant/message. The v3 scripted log stops at assistant/attempt.

v3 assigned {{message:1}} to the system message because it had no user message. The complete turn allocates {{message:1}} to the prompt at inbox insert, {{message:2}} to the system message, {{message:3}} to the assistant message, matching the real v4 log order (user, system, runtime context, assistant).
The v3 request/header tool schema is kept as the {{tools}} token; the concrete schema sidecar (tool-schemas.1.expected.json) is not part of this fixture.

providerModelConvention.recommendation: Either extend the same {{provider}}/{{model}} mask to these two provider-identity locations, or make the P0 replay route report fake/fake. Decide before wiring the Zig comparison.

replay.shape: calls[i].index is the 1-based model-call number; calls[i].stream is an AssistantStreamRecord[] identical in shape to assistant/attempt.data.stream.
replay.expansion: expandAssistantStream (assistant-stream.ts:202-230) turns the text-chunks row into one text-delta(index 0, text hi) and the raw chunk row into finish(stop).
replay.finish: The script carries an explicit finish chunk. The v3 attempt stream has none; a real v4 completed message records one (v4 log line 16), and llm-replay rejects a recorded call whose last chunk is not finish (llm-replay/src/index.ts:462-496). The dsh assembler would default to stop at EOF (assembler.ts:186-189), but the explicit chunk removes ambiguity.

openIssues: request/context.provider/model and assistant/message.source.provider/model are provider-route identity. The task convention masks only request/header config.provider/model, so under design decision 5 (fixed provider junclaw) these two locations will not match the fixture fake/fake unless the comparison is extended or the replay route reports fake/fake.

The v3 source is a scripted fake-ACP log, not a real dsh turn: it stops at assistant/attempt and has no user/message, inbox splice, request/context, step/end or turn/end. The complete v4 sequence is reconstructed from the real v4 log; every added event is listed in v3ToV4Differences. If the P0 harness does not yet emit inbox/request-context events, compare the implemented subset or split the fixture.

The request/header tools token {{tools}} comes from the v3 scripted fixture (tool t1). P0 is a no-tool turn; if the native harness advertises no tools, expected line 11 must drop the tools field (agent.ts:629 omits it when tools.length is 0).

The v4 ground-truth assistant stream also carries block-start/block-end and usage chunks from the deepseek provider. This fixture intentionally uses the delta-only replay stream (text-chunks + finish); the dsh assembler supports delta-only protocols (assembler.ts:33-35), but the expected stream is not byte-identical to the deepseek stream.
createdAt 200 is copied from the v3 fixture for readability. The comparison normalizer zeroes it (normalize.ts:387-388); a raw byte comparison without normalization would fail.
